category: Phrasal verbs on regular bases: D-F

entries.meaning: To do something occasionally as a hobby, without taking it seriously. ---
examples: He dabbles in photography on the weekends.
She dabbled in local politics for a year and quit.
They have been dabbling in real estate since the move.
entries.separable: inseparable — dabble in photography, dabble in it; never ✗ dabble photography in.
entries.forms: dabble in · dabbled in · dabbled in

entries.meaning: To write or produce something very quickly and without much care. ---
examples: Let me dash off a quick email before we leave.
She dashed the whole report off in under an hour.
He has dashed off three drafts since breakfast.
entries.separable: separable — dash off a note / dash a note off, and with a pronoun it must split: dash it off.
entries.forms: dash off · dashed off · dashed off

entries.meaning: To have existed since a particular time in the past. ---
examples: The church dates back to 1740.
Their argument dated back thirty years.
We found letters dating back to the war.
entries.separable: no object — nothing can come between the two words; the time follows to: dates back to 1740.
entries.forms: date back · dated back · dated back

entries.meaning: To become suddenly clear to someone. ---
examples: It finally dawned on me that she had been joking.
The truth dawns on him a little late every time.
It was dawning on all of us that the power was not coming back.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows on: it dawned on me, never ✗ it dawned me on. The subject is almost always it plus a that-clause.
entries.forms: dawn on · dawned on · dawned on

entries.meaning: To decorate something or dress someone in a showy way. ---
examples: They deck out the square with lights every December.
We decked the whole porch out for Halloween.
The lobby was decked out in red and gold.
entries.separable: separable — deck out the hall / deck the hall out, and deck it out. Most often passive: decked out in.
entries.forms: deck out · decked out · decked out

entries.meaning: To actually do what you promised or were expected to do. ---
examples: The new manager delivered on every promise he made.
Can a team that small deliver on a deadline like that?
The company has never delivered on its pledge to cut prices.
entries.separable: inseparable — deliver on a promise, deliver on it; never ✗ deliver a promise on.
entries.forms: deliver on · delivered on · delivered on

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere in large numbers, usually without being invited. ---
examples: Tourists descend on the town every July.
Reporters descended on the courthouse within the hour.
Relatives have been descending on the house all week.
entries.русский: наводнять, наводнить (о толпе); сваливаться, свалиться (на кого-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — the place or person follows on: descended on the town, never ✗ descended the town on.
entries.forms: descend on · descended on · descended on

entries.meaning: To reduce something that has gone too far. ---
examples: Let us dial back the sarcasm a little.
They dialed the pressure back after the first week.
He has dialed back his hours since the surgery.
entries.separable: separable — dial back the rhetoric / dial the rhetoric back, and dial it back.
entries.forms: dial back · dialed back · dialed back

entries.meaning: To make something less loud, less bright, or less intense. ---
examples: Could you dial down the drama for one evening?
She dialed the lights down for the movie.
They are dialing down expectations for the quarter.
entries.separable: separable — dial down the volume / dial the volume down, and dial it down.
entries.forms: dial down · dialed down · dialed down

entries.meaning: To adjust something until it is working exactly right. ---
examples: It took two hours to dial in the espresso grind.
He dialed the suspension in the night before the race.
The lighting is finally dialed in.
entries.separable: separable — dial in the settings / dial the settings in, and dial it in. Very often passive: the recipe is dialed in.
entries.forms: dial in · dialed in · dialed in

entries.meaning: To join a meeting by phone or conference line instead of in person. ---
examples: Three of us will dial in from Denver.
She dialed in about five minutes late.
He is dialing in from the airport again.
entries.русский: подключаться, подключиться по телефону (к совещанию); созваниваться, созвониться
entries.separable: no object — nothing sits between the two words; the meeting follows to: dial in to the call.
entries.forms: dial in · dialed in · dialed in

entries.meaning: To increase something deliberately. ---
examples: The coach wants to dial up the pressure in the second half.
They dialed the marketing up before the holidays.
He has dialed up the intensity since the trade.
entries.separable: separable — dial up the pressure / dial the pressure up, and dial it up.
entries.forms: dial up · dialed up · dialed up

entries.meaning: To grow fainter and fainter until it can no longer be heard. ---
examples: The applause slowly died away.
Voices die away as you walk deeper into the canyon.
The engine noise was dying away down the valley.
entries.separable: no object — the noise died away; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: die away · died away · died away

entries.meaning: To become much weaker, quieter, or calmer. ---
examples: The wind died down around midnight.
Wait until the noise dies down before you call.
The story has died down since the apology.
entries.separable: no object — the wind died down; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: die down · died down · died down

entries.meaning: To die one after another until few or none are left. ---
examples: The bees died off over the winter.
Whole orchards die off in a drought like this.
The last speakers of the dialect have been dying off for decades.
entries.русский: вымирать, вымереть (постепенно); гибнуть, погибнуть (один за другим)
entries.separable: no object — the bees died off; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: die off · died off · died off

entries.meaning: To disappear completely over time, leaving nothing of its kind. ---
examples: That custom died out fifty years ago.
Languages die out when children stop speaking them.
The breed had nearly died out by 1900.
entries.separable: no object — the custom died out; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: die out · died out · died out

entries.meaning: To eat a meal at a restaurant instead of at home. ---
examples: They dine out twice a month, always on a Friday.
We dined out every night of the trip.
Families have been dining out less since prices went up.
entries.русский: ужинать вне дома, поужинать в ресторане
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; nothing comes between the two words.
entries.forms: dine out · dined out · dined out

entries.meaning: To read or look at small parts of something rather than all of it. ---
examples: I dip into the cookbook whenever I need an idea.
She dipped into the memoir on the plane and put it down.
He has only dipped into the report so far.
entries.separable: inseparable — dip into a book, dip into it; never ✗ dip a book into.
entries.forms: dip into · dipped into · dipped into

entries.meaning: To spend part of money you had been keeping for something else. ---
examples: We had to dip into savings to fix the roof.
He dips into his bonus every December.
They have been dipping into the emergency fund all year.
entries.separable: inseparable — dip into savings, dip into it; never ✗ dip savings into.
entries.forms: dip into · dipped into · dipped into

entries.meaning: To hand something out freely, especially criticism, advice, or punishment. ---
examples: He dishes out advice nobody asked for.
The referee dished out four penalties in ten minutes.
He can dish it out, but he cannot take it.
entries.separable: separable — dish out advice / dish advice out, and with a pronoun it must split: dish it out.
entries.forms: dish out · dished out · dished out

entries.meaning: To serve food onto plates, or to serve up something ready-made. ---
examples: Grandma dished up three plates before anyone sat down.
I will dish up while the bread is still warm.
They are dishing up the same excuses as last year.
entries.separable: separable — dish up the pasta / dish the pasta up, and dish it up.
entries.forms: dish up · dished up · dished up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dish up the stew), intransitive (I will dish up while the bread is warm)

entries.meaning: To stop using or doing something because it is not necessary. ---
examples: Let us dispense with the introductions and get to work.
The judge dispensed with the usual formalities.
They have dispensed with paper tickets entirely.
entries.русский: обходиться, обойтись без; отказываться, отказаться от
entries.separable: inseparable — dispense with the formalities, dispense with them; never ✗ dispense them with.
entries.forms: dispense with · dispensed with · dispensed with

entries.meaning: To start doing something eagerly and without hesitating. ---
examples: Do not overthink it — just dive in.
She dived in on her first day and cleared the backlog.
They are diving in without a plan, as usual.
entries.русский: приниматься, приняться (с ходу); бросаться, броситься (в дело)
entries.separable: no object — just dive in; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: dive in · dived in · dived in

entries.meaning: To begin working on or examining something with great energy. ---
examples: Let us dive into the numbers before lunch.
He dived into the project and forgot to eat.
We have been diving into the archives all week.
entries.русский: погружаться, погрузиться (с головой во что-л.); браться, взяться (за что-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — dive into the numbers, dive into them; never ✗ dive the numbers into.
entries.forms: dive into · dived into · dived into

entries.meaning: To separate something into parts and share them out. ---
examples: We divided up the chores by floor.
Divide the class up into four groups.
The land has been divided up among the heirs.
entries.separable: separable — divide up the chores / divide the chores up, and divide them up.
entries.forms: divide up · divided up · divided up

entries.meaning: To share something out in portions among a group, informally. ---
examples: They divvied up the tips at closing.
Let us divvy the check up evenly.
The leftovers were divvied up before I got there.
entries.separable: separable — divvy up the tips / divvy the tips up, and divvy them up.
entries.forms: divvy up · divvied up · divvied up

entries.meaning: To give something out in small amounts, a little at a time. ---
examples: The office doles out parking passes one per floor.
He doled the candy out piece by piece.
Praise was doled out sparingly in that house.
entries.separable: separable — dole out the candy / dole the candy out, and dole it out.
entries.forms: dole out · doled out · doled out

entries.meaning: To dress someone, usually yourself, in showy, festive clothes. ---
examples: She dolls herself up for every family photo.
They got dolled up for prom.
The whole cast was dolled up in forties clothes.
entries.separable: separable, and nearly always reflexive or passive — doll herself up, get dolled up, all dolled up.
entries.forms: doll up · dolled up · dolled up

entries.meaning: To show someone a great deal of affection, often more than is good for them. ---
examples: He dotes on his granddaughter.
They doted on that dog for fifteen years.
She has always doted on her youngest.
entries.separable: inseparable — dote on the baby, dote on her; never ✗ dote her on.
entries.forms: dote on · doted on · doted on

entries.meaning: To turn around and go back the way you came. ---
examples: We doubled back when the trail flooded.
The road doubles back on itself twice.
He was doubling back to look for his keys.
entries.русский: возвращаться, вернуться тем же путём; поворачивать, повернуть назад
entries.separable: no object — we doubled back; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: double back · doubled back · doubled back

entries.meaning: To commit even harder to a course of action, especially a risky one, instead of backing off. ---
examples: Instead of apologizing, he doubled down.
The company is doubling down on electric models.
They have doubled down on a strategy that clearly is not working.
entries.русский: идти, пойти на обострение; удваивать, удвоить ставку (на что-л.)
entries.separable: no object — what you commit to follows on: double down on the plan. Nothing sits between the two words.
entries.forms: double down · doubled down · doubled down

entries.meaning: To bend forward sharply at the waist, from pain or laughter. ---
examples: He doubled over laughing at his own joke.
A cramp like that makes you double over fast.
They were doubled over with laughter by the end of it.
entries.separable: usually no object — he doubled over. When it does take one, the object splits the two words: the punch doubled him over.
entries.forms: double over · doubled over · doubled over
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (he doubled over), transitive (the punch doubled him over)

entries.meaning: To share a room, a bed, or a shift with someone because there is not enough to go around. ---
examples: The boys will double up in the back bedroom.
We doubled up on hotel rooms to save money.
Two nurses have been doubling up on nights all month.
entries.русский: селиться, поселиться вдвоём; делить, разделить (комнату, смену) с кем-л.
entries.separable: no object in this sense — double up in one room, double up on rooms; nothing sits between the two words.
entries.forms: double up · doubled up · doubled up

entries.meaning: To fall lightly asleep, usually without meaning to. ---
examples: He dozes off in front of the TV every night.
I dozed off for maybe ten minutes.
She was dozing off by the second act.
entries.separable: no object — he dozed off; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: doze off · dozed off · dozed off

entries.meaning: To make someone or something weaker, worse, or less successful. ---
examples: One bad quarter dragged down the whole year.
Do not let him drag you down with him.
Low turnout has been dragging down the numbers since March.
entries.separable: separable — drag down the average / drag the average down, and with a pronoun it must split: drag you down.
entries.forms: drag down · dragged down · dragged down

entries.meaning: To involve someone in a situation they want no part of. ---
examples: Do not drag me into your argument with your brother.
She was dragged into a lawsuit over a fence.
He keeps dragging the kids into it.
entries.separable: the person always sits between the two parts — drag me into this, never ✗ drag into me this.
entries.forms: drag into · dragged into · dragged into

entries.meaning: To continue for far longer than it should. ---
examples: The meeting dragged on for three hours.
Negotiations drag on every spring.
The trial has been dragging on since March.
entries.separable: no object — the meeting dragged on; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: drag on · dragged on · dragged on

entries.meaning: To make something last much longer than it needs to. ---
examples: They dragged out the goodbyes for an hour.
Do not drag it out — just tell her.
The case is being dragged out on purpose.
entries.separable: separable — drag out the goodbyes / drag the goodbyes out, and drag it out.
entries.forms: drag out · dragged out · dragged out

entries.meaning: To get information or an admission from someone who does not want to give it. ---
examples: It took an hour to drag the whole story out of him.
She dragged an apology out of her brother at the table.
I am tired of dragging answers out of that office.
entries.separable: separable, and it must split — what you extract sits in the middle: drag the truth out of him, drag it out of her; ✗ drag out of him the truth is impossible.
entries.forms: drag out of · dragged out of · dragged out of
entries.third person: drags out of · -ing form: dragging out of

entries.meaning: To mention something from the past that other people would rather forget. ---
examples: Why drag up what happened in 2009?
He dragged my old job up in front of everyone.
She keeps dragging up the same argument.
entries.separable: separable — drag up the past / drag the past up, and drag it up.
entries.forms: drag up · dragged up · dragged up

entries.meaning: To bring back a forgotten memory or old story, usually an unpleasant one. ---
examples: The article dredged up a scandal from the eighties.
Therapy dredges up things you thought were buried.
He has dredged up every mistake she ever made.
entries.separable: separable — dredge up an old scandal / dredge an old scandal up, and dredge it up.
entries.forms: dredge up · dredged up · dredged up

entries.meaning: To scold someone severely, often in front of other people. ---
examples: The coach dressed him down in front of the whole team.
She dresses down anyone who shows up late.
He was dressed down by his own lawyer.
entries.separable: separable — dress down the whole crew / dress the whole crew down, and with a pronoun it must split: dress him down.
entries.forms: dress down · dressed down · dressed down

entries.meaning: To wear clothes that are more casual than the occasion usually calls for. ---
examples: Everyone dresses down on Fridays.
He dressed down for the interview and regretted it.
They have been dressing down since the office went hybrid.
entries.separable: no object — everyone dresses down on Fridays; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: dress down · dressed down · dressed down

entries.meaning: To make something look or sound better than it really is. ---
examples: You cannot dress up a bad quarter with nice charts.
He dressed the résumé up with invented titles.
The proposal has been dressed up as a compromise.
entries.русский: приукрашивать, приукрасить; подавать в выгодном свете
entries.separable: separable — dress up the numbers / dress the numbers up, and dress it up.
entries.forms: dress up · dressed up · dressed up

entries.meaning: To put on a costume so as to look like someone or something else. ---
examples: The kids dress up as superheroes every October.
He dressed up as Lincoln for the school assembly.
They are dressing the dog up again.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — dress up the kids / dress the kids up, dress them up; with no object, dress up as a pirate.
entries.forms: dress up · dressed up · dressed up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (dress up as a pirate), transitive (dress the kids up)

entries.meaning: To put on nicer clothes than you usually wear. ---
examples: You do not have to dress up — it is just pizza.
She dressed up for her first day at the firm.
We were all dressed up with nowhere to go.
entries.separable: no object in this sense, or a reflexive one — dress up for dinner, dress yourself up.
entries.forms: dress up · dressed up · dressed up

entries.meaning: To slowly become less close to someone until the friendship fades. ---
examples: We drifted apart after college.
Couples drift apart when nobody is paying attention.
They had been drifting apart for years before the divorce.
entries.русский: отдаляться, отдалиться (друг от друга); расходиться, разойтись
entries.separable: no object — we drifted apart; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: drift apart · drifted apart · drifted apart

entries.meaning: To fall asleep gradually. ---
examples: I drifted off during the second half.
He drifts off the minute the car starts moving.
She was drifting off when the phone rang.
entries.separable: no object — I drifted off; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: drift off · drifted off · drifted off

entries.meaning: To talk in a dull, flat voice for far too long. ---
examples: He droned on about parking for twenty minutes.
She drones on whenever that topic comes up.
The speaker was still droning on when we left.
entries.separable: no object — the topic follows about: drone on about taxes. Nothing sits between the two words.
entries.forms: drone on · droned on · droned on

entries.meaning: To visit briefly, usually without arranging it first. ---
examples: Drop by any time after six.
She dropped by with soup on Sunday.
I have been dropping by the shop on my way home.
entries.separable: nothing can come between the two words. A place may follow straight after — drop by the office — but never ✗ drop the office by.
entries.forms: drop by · dropped by · dropped by
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (drop by tonight), transitive (drop by the office)

entries.meaning: To visit someone briefly and without warning. ---
examples: Feel free to drop in on your way through town.
My neighbor dropped in twice yesterday.
They are dropping in on us this weekend.
entries.separable: no object — the person visited follows on: drop in on your aunt, never ✗ drop her in.
entries.forms: drop in · dropped in · dropped in

entries.meaning: To become less in number or amount. ---
examples: Sales dropped off right after the holidays.
Attendance drops off every August.
Donations have been dropping off since the spring.
entries.separable: no object — sales dropped off; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: drop off · dropped off · dropped off

entries.meaning: To fall asleep, especially without intending to. ---
examples: He dropped off before the movie ended.
The baby drops off faster in the car.
I was dropping off when the alarm went.
entries.separable: no object — he dropped off; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: drop off · dropped off · dropped off

entries.meaning: To take someone or something to a place and leave them there. ---
examples: I will drop off the package on my way downtown.
She drops the kids off at seven every morning.
He was dropped off at the wrong terminal.
entries.русский: подвозить, подвезти; завозить, завезти; высаживать, высадить
entries.separable: separable — drop off the kids / drop the kids off, and with a pronoun it must split: drop them off.
entries.forms: drop off · dropped off · dropped off

entries.meaning: To leave a school, course, or contest before finishing it. ---
examples: He dropped out in his junior year.
Two runners drop out every mile in heat like this.
She has dropped out of the program twice now.
entries.separable: no object — what you leave follows of: drop out of school, never ✗ drop school out.
entries.forms: drop out · dropped out · dropped out

entries.meaning: To be so loud that another sound cannot be heard. ---
examples: The band drowned out the announcement.
Traffic drowns him out on that corner.
Her voice was drowned out by the crowd.
entries.separable: separable — drown out the announcement / drown the announcement out, and with a pronoun it must split: drown him out.
entries.forms: drown out · drowned out · drowned out

entries.meaning: To force someone out of a group or a profession in disgrace. ---
examples: Two officers were drummed out of the department after the hearing.
The party is trying to drum her out before the convention.
They drummed him out for taking money from a contractor.
entries.separable: separable — drum out the troublemakers or drum the troublemakers out; with a pronoun it must split: drummed him out.
entries.forms: drum out · drummed out · drummed out

entries.meaning: To get support, business, or interest by working at it. ---
examples: They are drumming up business with free samples.
He drummed up enough votes to win the seat.
Support has been drummed up mostly online.
entries.separable: separable — drum up business / drum business up, and drum it up.
entries.forms: drum up · drummed up · drummed up

entries.meaning: To remove the water from the surface of something, or to get dry that way. ---
examples: Dry off before you come inside.
She dried the dog off in the garage.
The kids are drying off on the porch.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — dry off the dog / dry the dog off, dry him off; with no object, dry off first.
entries.forms: dry off · dried off · dried off
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dry the dog off), intransitive (dry off before you come in)

entries.meaning: To lose all its moisture, or to make something lose it. ---
examples: The soil dries out fast in August.
My hands dried out from all the soap.
We have been drying out the boots by the stove.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — dry out the boots / dry the boots out, dry them out; with no object, the soil dried out.
entries.forms: dry out · dried out · dried out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dry out the boots), intransitive (the soil dries out)

entries.meaning: To stop drinking alcohol long enough to become sober, usually in a clinic. ---
examples: He spent a month upstate drying out.
She dried out at a clinic in Arizona.
The doctor told him he cannot dry out on his own.
entries.русский: проходить, пройти курс от алкоголизма; завязывать, завязать с выпивкой
entries.separable: no object — he is drying out; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: dry out · dried out · dried out

entries.meaning: Of a supply of money, work, or interest: to stop coming altogether. ---
examples: Funding dried up after the first year.
Offers dry up fast once the season ends.
Their donations have been drying up since the scandal.
entries.русский: иссякать, иссякнуть; прекращаться, прекратиться (о потоке денег, заказов)
entries.separable: no object — a supply dries up on its own; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: dry up · dried up · dried up

entries.meaning: To lose all its water and become completely dry. ---
examples: The creek dries up every July.
The puddles dried up by noon.
The well has dried up twice this decade.
entries.separable: usually no object — the creek dried up. With an object it separates: the sun dried up the puddles / dried them up.
entries.forms: dry up · dried up · dried up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the creek dried up), transitive (the sun dried up the puddles)

entries.meaning: To leave a place quickly and quietly, hoping nobody notices. ---
examples: He ducked out before the speeches started.
I am going to duck out early today.
She has been ducking out at lunch to make calls.
entries.separable: no object — he ducked out; nothing can come between the two words.
entries.forms: duck out · ducked out · ducked out

entries.meaning: To avoid a duty or a commitment you had agreed to. ---
examples: You cannot duck out of jury duty that easily.
He ducked out of the family photo again.
They are always ducking out of cleanup.
entries.separable: inseparable — duck out of jury duty, duck out of it; never ✗ duck jury duty out of.
entries.forms: duck out of · ducked out of · ducked out of
entries.third person: ducks out of · -ing form: ducking out of

entries.meaning: To make something simpler in a way that throws away what mattered. ---
examples: Do not dumb down the explanation for them.
They dumbed the whole curriculum down.
The textbook has been dumbed down for the new edition.
entries.русский: упрощать, упростить (в ущерб содержанию); опошлять, опошлить
entries.separable: separable — dumb down the material / dumb the material down, and dumb it down.
entries.forms: dumb down · dumbed down · dumbed down

entries.meaning: To criticize someone harshly, or to unload your troubles onto them. ---
examples: The press dumped on the mayor all week.
Sorry for dumping on you — it has been a long day.
He dumps on whoever answers the phone.
entries.русский: набрасываться, наброситься (с критикой); сваливать, свалить (проблемы на кого-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — dump on the mayor, dump on me; never ✗ dump me on. A different pattern takes an object first: dump your problems on me.
entries.forms: dump on · dumped on · dumped on

entries.meaning: To bring something back into use after a long time unused. ---
examples: He dusted off his old résumé on Sunday night.
She dusts that recipe off every Thanksgiving.
They have dusted off a play from the eighties.
entries.separable: separable — dust off the old résumé / dust the old résumé off, and dust it off.
entries.forms: dust off · dusted off · dusted off

entries.meaning: To keep thinking or talking about something unpleasant for too long. ---
examples: Try not to dwell on it tonight.
He dwelled on that one mistake for months.
She has been dwelling on the diagnosis since Friday.
entries.русский: зацикливаться, зациклиться на; долго останавливаться, остановиться на
entries.separable: inseparable — dwell on the mistake, dwell on it; never ✗ dwell it on.
entries.forms: dwell on · dwelled on · dwelled on

entries.meaning: To start something slowly and gently instead of all at once. ---
examples: Give yourself a week to ease into the new schedule.
She eased into the job with almost no training.
He's easing into running again after the injury.
entries.русский: постепенно втягиваться, втянуться; входить в курс, войти в курс
entries.separable: inseparable — the object follows into: ease into the job, never ease the job into; only a reflexive comes first: ease yourself into it
